name: camel-case
remediation_notes: This 1.5K utility is small enough to vendor directly into your project. Most teams can copy the implementation in minutes. If you prefer a maintained alternative, switch to lodash.camelcase, though for such a focused utility vendoring usually makes more sense.

name: no-case
remediation_notes: Inlining is practical here—copy the ~1.5kLOC implementation into projects to eliminate the dependency on unmaintained code. With 2.5M dispersed dependents, coordinated migration to an alternative is infeasible.

name: ip-regex
remediation_notes: Zero dependencies and 553 LOC of stable regex patterns. Unmaintained but requires no changes; most consumers will simply pin the version. Adoption isn't practical at 2.4M dependents; vendoring fragments maintenance across the ecosystem.

name: ee-first
remediation_notes: No runtime dependencies and only 301 LOC means minimal supply chain risk; pin the version and audit if security scanning flags issues, but the stable API is unlikely to break with future Node.js versions.

name: param-case
remediation_notes: param-case has been dormant for 590 days with no active maintenance. Its 2.4M dependents are too distributed for adoption to be practical; most should switch to a maintained case-transformation package or inline the simple utility themselves.

name: path-type
remediation_notes: Trivial and unmaintained (259 LOC, zero runtime dependencies). Node.js provides identical functionality natively via fs.stat; the README itself recommends using native calls.

name: arrify
remediation_notes: Package's own README recommends switching to [value].flat(). For the null/undefined → empty array edge case, add a conditional if needed.

name: invert-kv
remediation_notes: Unmaintained but stable: no dependencies or native code. Pinning the version is the practical approach for 2.4M dependents.

name: lcid
remediation_notes: Dead for 2+ years but stable; 287 of 390 lines are static data. Copy the LCID-to-locale mapping into your project, or pin the version.

name: tsutils
remediation_notes: Unmaintained for 5 years; incompatibility will accumulate as TypeScript evolves. Dependents should migrate utilities to typescript's compiler API or vendor what's needed.

name: relateurl
remediation_notes: Stable, dependency-free utility with most usage concentrated in well-maintained html-minifier packages. Small codebase (588 LOC) and narrow scope make pinning the current version safe.

name: escalade
remediation_notes: Escalade is 73 lines with no dependencies—small enough that each dependent should copy it in and drop the unmaintained package. The algorithm is stable and unlikely to need future changes.

name: word-wrap
remediation_notes: Dependency-free and minimal (612 LOC)—suitable for vendoring or accepting with a pinned version. No upstream supply chain risk.

name: escodegen
remediation_notes: 2.3M dependents across the ecosystem with no maintenance for 3 years make coordinated migration impractical. The package is stable build-time code—pin the version and carry the risk.

name: css-select-base-adapter
remediation_notes: Copy this 318-line utility into your project. With zero runtime dependencies and a stable, minimal surface, vendoring it is safer than maintaining the external dependency.

name: is-core-module
remediation_notes: Stable, single-purpose utility acceptable to pin. Drop-in alternatives like Node's `module.builtinModules` exist but lack version-checking support that some tooling consumers need.

name: unquote
remediation_notes: Unmaintained for 8+ years, but the code is trivial—93 lines, zero dependencies, single purpose. Vendor the function into your project rather than depend on abandoned software.

name: inherits
remediation_notes: A stable, minimal utility for prototypal inheritance. No vulnerabilities or dependency risks; last meaningful release was 7+ years ago because the code is complete. Most of the 2.3M dependents treat it as pinned stable code and never touch it.

name: encodeurl
remediation_notes: Small utility (531 LOC, zero dependencies) with stable API and no maintained replacement. Copy the code into your project to remove the dormant dependency.

name: prop-types
remediation_notes: Archived but stable. No maintenance needed; pin the version. Existing code works unchanged. Modern projects should use TypeScript for type safety instead.

name: get-stream
remediation_notes: The package is stable and small enough (1758 lines) for each dependent to copy into their own codebase, removing dependency on dead code.

name: normalize-path
remediation_notes: Small, focused utility with zero runtime dependencies and eight years of stable operation. The self-contained 217-line implementation is suitable for inlining—consuming projects can vendor the code to eliminate the unmaintained dependency concern without introducing new risk.

name: side-channel
remediation_notes: 2.3M dependent repos rely on this stable utility library for side-channel storage; no clear maintained alternative exists. Pin the version and monitor for issues, but forking is unnecessary unless bugs emerge.

name: text-table
remediation_notes: Text table formatting is stable functionality in a small, dependency-free package. Vendoring the code into consuming projects is practical for the 2.2M scattered dependents and eliminates the unmaintained dependency risk.

name: astral-regex
remediation_notes: Unmaintained since 2019 but only 114 lines and zero dependencies—copy the regex pattern directly into any consuming project rather than maintain the external dependency.

name: is-stream
remediation_notes: A zero-dependency utility for a stable problem (Node.js stream detection). With 337 LoC and no runtime deps, the risk of keeping it pinned is low; the risk of each of 2.3M dependents vendoring or forking their own version is higher.

name: parse-json
remediation_notes: parse-json wraps JSON.parse with better error formatting (code frames + line numbers). At 451 LOC with trivial complexity, inlining is viable; 2.26M repos across thousands of packages rules out coordinated maintenance. Dormancy is safe here—JSON.parse is stable and rarely breaks.

name: dom-converter
remediation_notes: Essentially all usage flows through renderkid. The code is tiny (153 LoC) and carries a dead transitive dependency (utila). Inline it into renderkid and drop the dependency.

name: pretty-error
remediation_notes: Error-formatting utility stable for 4+ years with no security issues or known bugs. Code is small (510 LoC) and could be vendored, but pinning the version is practical for this broad set of dependents.

name: renderkid
remediation_notes: Renderkid is in heavy transitive use through pretty-error (64.5M downloads). The package is small, stable, and specialized—no HTML/CSS-to-terminal alternative exists. The pretty-error maintainer should adopt it or nominate a community maintainer.

name: acorn-globals
remediation_notes: Stable utility unmaintained for 1334 days; 2.2M dependent repos make collective migration impractical. Pin version, monitor acorn compatibility for future releases.

name: import-from
remediation_notes: Unmaintained for 4+ years but stable; 142 lines with zero dependencies and no breaking changes in sight. Pin the version and use it as-is, or vendor the trivial code if reducing dependencies matters to your project.

name: redent
remediation_notes: Ultra-simple, stable utility with no security issues. Pin the version; the code is too small to warrant forking and too widely used to ask all dependents to switch to the underlying libraries.

name: utila
remediation_notes: utila is archived with no commits in 11+ years, but the code is small (428 LOC) and has no runtime dependencies. dom-converter (57.5M downloads) accounts for essentially all usage and should inline the code rather than carry an unmaintained transitive dependency.

name: duplexer
remediation_notes: Package is explicitly deprecated ("Do not use" in README) and unmaintained since 2019. The 187-line codebase has no runtime dependencies and is simple enough to copy into your project or replace with standard Node.js streams API.

name: glob-to-regexp
remediation_notes: Replace with minimatch, the maintained standard for glob matching in Node.js. Handles the same patterns (simple globs, extended globs, globstars) and is already in most dependency trees.

name: clone-deep
remediation_notes: Switch to lodash (_.cloneDeep) for a maintained alternative, or use native structuredClone() for modern Node/browser runtimes.

name: is-arguments
remediation_notes: This is a stable, niche utility for detecting JavaScript arguments objects—a problem that doesn't change. Pin a working version; the small codebase and 2.2M dependents suggest it's reliable. Modern code avoids arguments objects, making the maintenance burden minimal.

name: object-is
remediation_notes: Object.is is built-in to JavaScript; this 485-LOC shim is small and stable enough to inline rather than carry a dormant dependency. A recent release (41d ago) despite 790d since the last commit suggests passive maintenance, but the code won't change.

name: mem
remediation_notes: Stable, focused memoization library with 2.2M transitive dependents. Simple codebase (1565 LOC) unlikely to develop critical issues; version-pin to manage risk. Migration is per-project only if advisory is relevant to your use case.

name: uglify-js
remediation_notes: Unmaintained parser and minifier with vast reach (2.2M dependent repositories). Minification use cases should migrate to terser; bundling/build integration should use esbuild or swc; advanced transformation should evaluate specialized tools per use case. 2 unpatched security advisories present risk.

name: util-deprecate
remediation_notes: Only 131 lines of code providing a simple deprecation function—in Node.js it re-exports util.deprecate(), in browsers a basic polyfill. With 2.2M dependents, inlining this trivial utility avoids maintaining a 10-year-stale external dependency.

name: type-check
remediation_notes: Stable runtime type checker with minimal code (177 LOC) serving a fragmented ecosystem. Pin the version and switch only if new JS features aren't supported or you need a heavier validation framework.

name: wordwrap
remediation_notes: Unmaintained since 2015 but functionally complete; vast majority of usage is transitive through build tools where pinning is pragmatic.

name: combined-stream
remediation_notes: Dead for 7 years, but the 168-LOC implementation is stable and ubiquitous. Migrate to combined-stream2 (streams2-compatible drop-in replacement mentioned in the README) or vendor the minimal code.

name: delayed-stream
remediation_notes: 85 lines of straightforward stream-buffering logic with zero dependencies. Copy directly into consuming projects rather than maintaining a dependency for what amounts to a few event buffer operations.

name: reusify
remediation_notes: No external dependencies eliminate supply chain risk; distributed across 2.1M repos makes coordinated migration impractical; pin the version and monitor for critical issues.

name: strict-uri-encode
remediation_notes: At 84 lines with no dependencies, copy the code directly into your project. If RFC 3986 strictness isn't essential, consider using native encodeURIComponent instead.

name: shallow-clone
remediation_notes: Small, self-contained utility that's safe to inline. Dormancy is not a risk factor for a mature package with no dead transitive dependencies and no security surface.

name: function-bind
remediation_notes: Completed polyfill for a standard feature now universally available in all JavaScript environments. Zero dependencies, zero maintenance burden, zero security risk. Dormancy is expected and safe.

name: has
remediation_notes: Trivial utility that checks hasOwnProperty (6 lines). Copy the implementation into your codebase or replace with Object.hasOwn() in modern projects (ES2022+).

name: safer-buffer
remediation_notes: Unmaintained polyfill for the Buffer API on ancient Node.js versions. Small surface and no runtime deps make it low-risk to pin. Most projects should remove it and use native Buffer.alloc()/Buffer.from(); the minority still supporting Node <4.5 can safely accept the pinned version.

name: cssom
remediation_notes: Stable CSS parser with no known security issues or maintenance burden. Most dependents can safely pin the version indefinitely. Switch to PostCSS only if you need CSS transformation features like minification or reformatting.

name: xml-name-validator
remediation_notes: 7 lines implementing W3C spec productions, zero runtime deps, no maintenance needed. Copy into your codebase; it's smaller than the dependency overhead and removes supply chain risk.

name: is-binary-path
remediation_notes: 108-line utility checking file extensions against a list. Small enough that each dependent can safely copy the code and drop the dependency.

name: kleur
remediation_notes: Unmaintained for nearly 4 years but foundational to millions of projects. Chalk is actively maintained and API-compatible. Most projects should migrate; vendoring is possible for special cases but creates distributed technical debt.

name: symbol-tree
remediation_notes: At 465 LOC with zero dependencies, this stable tree structure is small enough that dependents should copy it into their own codebase rather than maintain an unmaintained external dependency. Six years of dormancy with no security issues suggests the API is complete.

name: natural-compare
remediation_notes: Stable code (308 lines, low complexity) with no dependencies. Dormant for 564+ days but no security risk. 2.1M dependents distributed widely—no single steward. For most, pin the version; natural sorting is solved here.

name: kind-of
remediation_notes: Stable type-checking utility with no dependencies and 2M+ dependents; forking impractical. Pin version and audit against any disclosed security issues.

name: stack-utils
remediation_notes: Stack-utils is unmaintained for 3.5 years but foundational for 2.1M Node.js repos. Small (1.6k LOC), stable, single maintained dependency. Needs ecosystem-level adoption: either community fork or Node.js integration.

name: once
remediation_notes: Dormant but stable and tested at scale (2.1M dependents). Simple, low-complexity utility with minimal risk. Pinning and acceptance is pragmatic over coordinating ecosystem-wide replacement.

name: whatwg-encoding
remediation_notes: This package is archived and superseded by @exodus/bytes, which is more spec compliant and faster. Switch to @exodus/bytes—jsdom itself uses it.

name: picocolors
remediation_notes: Package is feature-complete with no runtime dependencies and minimal code. Dormancy reflects stability, not abandonment; switching 2.1M dependents is impractical. Pin the version and accept the risk.

name: infer-owner
remediation_notes: The implementation is straightforward filesystem walking with caching—small enough to vendor directly without burden, and safer than pinning a package unmaintained since 2019.

name: detect-newline
remediation_notes: Package is 138 lines with zero runtime dependencies and detects dominant newline characters. Simple enough to copy directly into consuming projects, eliminating the unmaintained dependency entirely.

name: wrappy
remediation_notes: Wrappy wraps functions while preserving their properties. At 143 lines with zero dependencies, it's stable enough to pin or simple enough to copy directly into your project if you want to drop the dependency.

name: gzip-size
remediation_notes: Unmaintained for 4.4 years but functionally stable with minimal complexity; safe to pin or vendor the 285-line codebase.

name: isarray
remediation_notes: Drop this dependency entirely. Array.isArray has been native since ES5 (2009) and available in all modern JavaScript environments; use the built-in directly instead.

name: throat
remediation_notes: 2M+ dependents on this 3+ year old package. Switch to p-limit (actively maintained, similar concurrency-limiting API). Vendor also viable due to small size (998 LOC, no deps).

name: aria-query
remediation_notes: Stable data package wrapping the W3C ARIA 1.2 spec. No runtime dependencies. Pin the version and monitor for ARIA spec updates; fork it (adopt) if critical issues emerge later.

name: queue-microtask
remediation_notes: Standard queueMicrotask is now universally available. Copy the ~10-line fallback pattern into your codebase if you need Node.js 10 support; otherwise use the native API directly and drop the dependency.

name: prompts
remediation_notes: Prompts is dormant with 2 dead transitive dependencies creating security and compatibility risk. Switch to inquirer (feature-rich) or clack (minimal, modern). API patterns are similar; most migrations are straightforward.

name: sisteransi
remediation_notes: Only 85 lines of stable ANSI escape code helpers. Vendoring (copying inline) is safe and recommended for the 2M+ dependents to eliminate dependency risk entirely.

name: pirates
remediation_notes: Pirates is 82 lines with no runtime dependencies—copy it into your project to eliminate dependence on unmaintained code.

name: merge-stream
remediation_notes: At 112 lines with zero runtime dependencies, this stable utility is small enough to inline directly into consuming projects. Six years without maintenance is acceptable for such focused, simple code.

name: path-is-absolute
remediation_notes: This package is a deprecated ponyfill for Node.js 0.12's path.isAbsolute(), which is now built into Node's standard path module with the same API on all supported versions. Dependents should use Node's native path module instead.

name: object-assign
remediation_notes: Package is deprecated and unmaintained; maintainers explicitly recommend native `Object.assign()` available in Node 4+ and all modern browsers.

name: strip-bom
remediation_notes: The entire implementation is 22 lines with no dependencies and doesn't change. Vendors should inline the code rather than depend on an unmaintained package.

name: escape-string-regexp
remediation_notes: Switch to the native RegExp.escape() API where feasible. For projects needing backward compatibility, the implementation is simple enough to inline directly.

name: axobject-query
remediation_notes: With only 2.2k LOC and zero runtime dependencies, this stable Chrome AXObject query utility is practical to vendor directly into consuming projects. Codelyzer drives 99.6% of usage; other dependents can fork or inline the code for independence from unmaintained upstream.

name: damerau-levenshtein
remediation_notes: With zero runtime dependencies and only 194 lines of JavaScript, consumers should copy the implementation directly into their codebase. The Damerau-Levenshtein algorithm is simple enough that each project can inline it with minimal duplication.

name: browser-process-hrtime
remediation_notes: This 69-line polyfill is stable but unmaintained. Projects should vendor the code or use the browser standard performance.now().

name: ast-types-flow
remediation_notes: Flow is unmaintained; projects should migrate to TypeScript for static typing or use AST types from their tooling directly (e.g., @babel/types).

name: @hapi/hoek
remediation_notes: Stable, dormant utility library with zero runtime dependencies and 2M+ dispersed dependents. Pin the version and monitor advisories; wholesale replacement or vendoring is impractical at this scale.

name: punycode
remediation_notes: Punycode is maintained as a built-in module in Node.js. For Node.js users, replace the npm dependency with `require('punycode')` (use the built-in). Non-Node.js environments need an alternative package.

name: minimist
remediation_notes: Dormant with 2 unresolved advisories. Migrate to yargs, commander, or minimist-lite—all actively maintained, with the latter a direct fork.

name: eslint-plugin-react
remediation_notes: Widely-used ESLint plugin for React; 2M+ dependents distributed across the ecosystem. Minimally maintained but stable; no direct replacement exists that covers the full rule set. Pin versions and monitor for security issues.

name: whatwg-fetch
remediation_notes: Dormant polyfill now safe to keep—modern browsers implement fetch natively, so this code doesn't execute. Pin the version if supporting old browsers; otherwise harmless.

name: is-generator-fn
remediation_notes: Unmaintained for 4.7 years but small enough (121 LOC, no dependencies) that dependents should vendor the code directly. The check itself is trivial to replicate without the dependency.

name: clone
remediation_notes: Explicitly deprecated and unmaintained since 2018 (last release), but stable with zero runtime dependencies. The package itself is low-risk; dependents should migrate to native structuredClone() for modern runtimes or maintained alternatives like lodash.cloneDeep depending on compatibility needs.

name: jsx-ast-utils
remediation_notes: Widely-adopted utility for JSX AST analysis. Feature-complete and stable with no security issues or active bugs. Pin the version and monitor for Node/Babel compatibility changes.

name: mkdirp
remediation_notes: Replace with Node.js built-in fs.mkdir or fs.promises.mkdir with {recursive: true} option, available since v10.12.0. Eliminates an unmaintained dependency for functionality now in the standard library.

name: p-defer
remediation_notes: At 134 lines with no dependencies, vendoring the code is practical for any project. Modern JavaScript/TypeScript should use native Promise.withResolvers() instead (available in TS 5.4+).

name: p-is-promise
remediation_notes: Unmaintained 5+ years but trivially inlineable—the core logic is a few lines checking instanceof Promise. Observable-to-promise drives 95% of usage but even small projects can afford to copy the code.

name: @hapi/topo
remediation_notes: @hapi/joi and @hapi/validate account for 60% of direct usage and support 1.93M transitive dependents; both should vendor this 165-line utility to simplify the dependency graph.

name: path-parse
remediation_notes: Package is stable and unmaintained (226 LOC, no activity in 1800 days). Node.js's built-in path.parse satisfies the original ponyfill purpose; for older Node versions, inlining the minimal code eliminates dependency risk.

name: cross-spawn
remediation_notes: No active vulnerabilities; 182 lines of stable code solving specific Windows spawn issues. Pin to a working version and accept the unmaintained status.

name: has-symbols
remediation_notes: has-symbols is a stable, dependency-free utility for detecting Symbol support. Most dependents should pin the version; many can remove it entirely since Symbol is now ubiquitous in modern JavaScript environments.

name: jest-pnp-resolver
remediation_notes: Jest's default resolver has supported PnP natively since v24.4.0 (2019). Upgrade Jest and remove this package from your config to use the built-in resolver.

name: shebang-regex
remediation_notes: This package is a single shebang regex with no dependencies—trivial to copy inline into any project. Since it's dormant but the functionality is stable, vendoring the pattern eliminates an unmaintained dependency without risk.

name: randombytes
remediation_notes: Stable, minimal utility with unchanged crypto APIs. Pin the version; for direct dependents, migrating to native crypto.getRandomValues is feasible but not urgent.

name: shebang-command
remediation_notes: Unmaintained since 2019 but code is extremely stable—only 112 lines with no breaking changes likely. Vendoring inline is practical, or keep with version pin. Note it has one runtime dependency (shebang-regex) that would also need evaluation.

name: address
remediation_notes: Pin the version. No runtime dependencies, 256 LOC, stable code. Most of the 1.88M dependents are transitive. Direct users can safely accept the dormancy or switch to Node's built-in os.networkInterfaces() or internal-ip.

name: case-sensitive-paths-webpack-plugin
remediation_notes: Pin to latest—small and stable with no dependencies. Plan Webpack v5+ upgrades long-term for better built-in module resolution.

name: micromatch
remediation_notes: Micromatch was built as a faster alternative to minimatch; with micromatch unmaintained for 1.8M+ dependents, switching back to minimatch or evaluating picomatch is realistic for most consumers of this glob-matching library.

name: object.fromentries
remediation_notes: Pin the current version; Object.fromEntries is standard ES2019 and shipped everywhere. If your project doesn't support pre-ES2019 environments, remove the dependency—the native implementation is better.

name: @svgr/core
remediation_notes: Dormant but stable, with 1.8M dependents and zero dead transitive dependencies. Large surface with multiple partial alternatives (CRA native SVG imports, svgo, babel plugins); versions are safe to pin for most use cases.

name: process-nextick-args
remediation_notes: process.nextTick() has natively supported arguments since Node.js 0.10 (2013). Eliminate the dependency by calling the native API directly instead of through this unmaintained wrapper.

name: aggregate-error
remediation_notes: JavaScript's built-in `AggregateError` (available in Node.js 15+, now standard) provides identical functionality; migrate to the native API and remove the dependency.

name: @svgr/webpack
remediation_notes: Dormant webpack loader for a declining bundler. Plan to migrate to Vite or other modern alternatives; if staying on webpack, pin the version and accept the risk.

name: media-typer
remediation_notes: Last release was 7 years ago but implementation is stable (RFC 6838) and dependency-free. At 179 lines with zero runtime deps, inlining is practical. Alternatively, pin the version and accept the dormant dependency.

name: type-is
remediation_notes: A focused utility for HTTP content-type inference. No releases in 13 months reflects stability, not abandonment; it's still maintained by an active contributor. Safe to depend on with a pinned version.

name: object.entries
remediation_notes: Object.entries is stable and native in all modern JavaScript (Node 6+, all current browsers). The polyfill is safe pinned but unnecessary for most projects—drop it unless you explicitly support IE11 or legacy Node.

name: node-fetch
remediation_notes: Switch to Node's native Fetch API for Node 18+ projects. For older versions, pin this package version and plan migration when Node is upgraded.

name: @istanbuljs/load-nyc-config
remediation_notes: Configuration utility tightly coupled to NYC coverage tool; small stable codebase (694 LOC) with 6-year release dormancy. Pin the version and monitor NYC for breaking config format changes.

name: find-cache-dir
remediation_notes: This 250-line utility for finding node_modules/.cache/ directories is simple and stable enough to inline. With 1.8M dependents and a stalled maintainer, projects should copy the function into their own code rather than depend on unmaintained code.

name: @sinonjs/commons
remediation_notes: A pure utility library used almost entirely by maintained Sinon testing packages (lolex, formatio). Stable enough to pin the version; no maintenance burden due to absence of side effects or external API dependencies.

name: object-hash
remediation_notes: Dormant but small (4.6K LOC) and stable. With 1.8M dependent repos, no ecosystem steward is feasible. Pin the version and monitor; vendoring is viable if security issues emerge.

name: estraverse
remediation_notes: Estraverse is stable infrastructure code—no runtime dependencies, small focused surface, and unchanged ES262 traversal semantics for 4.5 years. Switching 1.8M dependents to an alternative is impractical and unnecessary; the risk comes from its dependents' own changes, not estraverse itself.

name: run-parallel
remediation_notes: This 437-line utility is straightforward to inline with minimal dependencies. With 1.8M dependent repos and no maintenance activity, dependents should vendor the code rather than maintaining an external dependency on unmaintained upstream.

name: node-notifier
remediation_notes: Cross-platform desktop notification library with 1.7M dependent repos. At 548 LoC with no native code, this is small enough for each project to copy into their codebase and drop the dependency entirely, avoiding the security advisory and maintenance burden.

name: negotiator
remediation_notes: Pin the version. A tiny, dependency-free implementation of a stable algorithm needs no active maintenance—dormancy here carries minimal risk.

name: string.prototype.trimstart
remediation_notes: String.prototype.trimStart is a standard ES2019 feature with native support across all modern runtimes. The package is dormant but stable with strong test coverage. For modern targets, the native feature makes the dependency obsolete; for legacy support, pin the version and carry minimal risk.

name: string.prototype.trimend
remediation_notes: This package polyfills String.prototype.trimEnd, which is universally supported in modern JavaScript (ES2019+). Dependents can safely drop the dependency and use the native method directly; for projects requiring pre-ES2019 support, pin the version rather than seeking updates.

name: esutils
remediation_notes: Foundational utility library that has reached stability—ES5 predicates don't age. No active maintenance needed. Pin the version.

name: @svgr/plugin-jsx
remediation_notes: Dormant but stable SVGR plugin. Pin the version. For updates or fixes, check the parent SVGR project or evaluate alternatives based on your use case.

name: @svgr/hast-util-to-babel-ast
remediation_notes: Dormant utility in the active SVGR ecosystem. 100% usage via @svgr/plugin-jsx (66M downloads/month). Stable, narrow purpose; pin version and monitor SVGR's broader health.

name: @svgr/babel-plugin-add-jsx-attribute
remediation_notes: Dormant but stable plugin with zero runtime dependencies. Nearly all usage flows through actively maintained @svgr/babel-preset. Accept the version lock; no alternative exists within SVGR's transformation pipeline.

name: @svgr/babel-plugin-replace-jsx-attribute-value
remediation_notes: Part of the maintained SVGR ecosystem (parent @svgr/babel-preset still ships 65M downloads/month). Zero runtime dependencies. Stable Babel plugin—pin the version and carry minimal risk.

name: @svgr/babel-plugin-remove-jsx-attribute
remediation_notes: 100% of usage flows through the maintained @svgr/babel-preset package. This Babel plugin is specialized and unlikely to need updates; pinning the version is safe.

name: @svgr/babel-preset
remediation_notes: The preset can be vendored into consuming packages to decouple from the unmaintained monorepo. Major users like @svgr/core should absorb the preset code rather than depend on a stalled project.

name: @svgr/babel-plugin-svg-em-dimensions
remediation_notes: Stable Babel plugin for SVG-to-React em dimension transformation. All real usage flows through @svgr/babel-preset; no maintenance needed for a solved problem. Pin and move on.

name: @svgr/babel-plugin-transform-svg-component
remediation_notes: No runtime dependencies; dormancy is benign for stable transformation code. Real risk lies upstream in @svgr/babel-preset maintenance. Safe to pin and monitor parent package health.

name: @svgr/babel-plugin-remove-jsx-empty-expression
remediation_notes: A stable Babel plugin with zero runtime dependencies that's part of SVGR. The lack of recent updates reflects code maturity—Babel's plugin API is stable and the transformation is correct. Dormancy is not abandonment.

name: @svgr/babel-plugin-transform-react-native-svg
remediation_notes: All real usage routes through @svgr/babel-preset (65M weekly downloads). Vendor the 11K LOC plugin into the preset to eliminate an unmaintained transitive dependency.

name: @svgr/babel-plugin-svg-dynamic-title
remediation_notes: This Babel plugin is only used transitively through @svgr/babel-preset, which is actively maintained. It's stable and feature-complete; pin the version or the parent preset version to manage risk.

name: @svgr/plugin-svgo
remediation_notes: This plugin wraps the maintained SVGO optimizer in 11K lines. Direct dependents should vendor the code to remove the unmaintained dependency; most consumers (87.7%) access it indirectly through @svgr/webpack anyway.

name: html-escaper
remediation_notes: Stable and dependency-free. HTML escaping is a solved problem—no active maintenance needed. Pin the version and monitor advisories.

name: saxes
remediation_notes: Saxes was archived as a stricter XML parser forked from sax 1.2.4. With 1.78M dependents spread across many projects, most should switch back to the original actively-maintained sax package. Projects relying on saxes' stricter parsing may need to vendor the 1822 LOC or evaluate other XML parsers.

name: on-finished
